title: English Course
description: An original structured en-US course for practical A1 and A2 communication.

levels.title: Beginner
levels.description: Build essential English for concrete everyday communication.
objectives: Communicate in familiar everyday situations with controlled language.

units.title: Meeting People
units.description: Greet people, exchange basic information, and complete a first introduction.
objectives: Introduce yourself and another person.
Ask and answer basic personal questions.
grammarTopics: subject pronouns
verb be
basic WH questions
yes/no questions with be
basic possessive adjectives
communicativeFunctions: greeting
introducing yourself
asking for basic information
closing a conversation

units.title: Numbers, Time & Dates
units.description: Use numbers, spelling, dates, and clock time to exchange practical details and arrange a meeting.
objectives: Say, understand, and use numbers from zero to one hundred in everyday exchanges.
Spell names and exchange a practice phone number and email address clearly.
grammarTopics: cardinal numbers 0–100
alphabet spelling and digit-by-digit numbers
What day/date and ordinal date forms
What time, o'clock, half past, and time prepositions
present simple with time expressions
integrated numbers, dates, time, and availability
communicativeFunctions: Say, understand, and use numbers from zero to one hundred in everyday exchanges.
Spell names and exchange a practice phone number and email address clearly.
Ask for and state weekdays, months, and simple calendar dates.
Ask for and tell common clock times.

units.title: Family & People
units.description: Identify family members, describe people, and express basic possession.
objectives: Name close family members and say how they are related.
Ask and answer who a person is in a photo or group.
grammarTopics: family nouns and possessive adjectives
Who is and demonstrative this
have with I/you/we/they and has with he/she/it
be and have for descriptions
possessive adjectives and apostrophe-s
integrated family description review
communicativeFunctions: Name close family members and say how they are related.
Ask and answer who a person is in a photo or group.
Say what people have and ask about family or personal features.
Give a short respectful description of a person's appearance and character.

units.title: Daily Life
units.description: Talk about routines, frequency, and simple present questions and negatives.
objectives: Describe the main actions in a typical day in sequence.
Use the present simple for regular actions and facts.
grammarTopics: present simple first-person routine verbs
present simple affirmative and third-person -s
do not and does not plus base verb
do/does questions and short answers
frequency adverbs before main verbs and after be
integrated present simple and frequency review
communicativeFunctions: Describe the main actions in a typical day in sequence.
Use the present simple for regular actions and facts.
Make clear present simple negative statements about routines.
Ask and answer present simple questions about regular activities.

units.title: Home & Around Town
units.description: Describe a home and neighborhood, locate places, and give short directions.
objectives: Name rooms and give a simple description of a home.
Say what exists in a room or neighborhood.
grammarTopics: be, have, and room nouns
there is for singular and there are for plural
where questions and place prepositions
place nouns and there is/are review
imperatives, turn, go straight, and location phrases
integrated town and direction review
communicativeFunctions: Name rooms and give a simple description of a home.
Say what exists in a room or neighborhood.
Ask for and state an object's location using basic prepositions.
Identify useful places and say where they are in town.

units.title: Food & Café English
units.description: Talk about food preferences and quantities and place a polite café order.
objectives: Name common foods and drinks and say what you eat or drink.
Distinguish items that can be counted from food substances and liquids.
grammarTopics: food nouns and present simple
a/an, plural nouns, and uncountable nouns
some in affirmatives and any in questions/negatives
like, don't like, and preference questions
would like as a fixed polite request
integrated café-order review
communicativeFunctions: Name common foods and drinks and say what you eat or drink.
Distinguish items that can be counted from food substances and liquids.
Ask about and describe available food with some and any.
Ask about and state food preferences.

units.title: Free Time & Abilities
units.description: Talk about hobbies, abilities, current activities, invitations, and simple plans.
objectives: Name hobbies and describe regular free-time activities.
Ask about and state basic abilities with can.
grammarTopics: like plus noun or to-infinitive
can/can't and ability questions
like/love/don't like plus activities
present continuous for actions now
let's and invitation responses
integrated free-time review
communicativeFunctions: Name hobbies and describe regular free-time activities.
Ask about and state basic abilities with can.
Compare simple likes and dislikes and ask about preferences.
Ask and say what is happening at the present moment.

units.title: Shopping & Everyday English
units.description: Discuss clothes, colors, sizes, prices, choices, help requests, and common problems.
objectives: Name basic clothing and describe its color.
Ask for a clothing size and understand a simple price.
grammarTopics: be plus color and clothing nouns
what size/how much and number review
this/that and one as a substitute noun
can/could requests in a store
be negative, doesn't work, and help requests
integrated A1 shopping and help review
communicativeFunctions: Name basic clothing and describe its color.
Ask for a clothing size and understand a simple price.
Compare and choose between nearby and more distant items.
Ask a store worker for an item, size, or fitting room politely.

levels.title: Elementary
levels.description: Extend basic English to connected everyday communication and problem solving.
objectives: Connect ideas and handle common everyday situations with increasing independence.

units.title: Talking About the Past
units.description: Describe past states and completed actions and ask what happened.
objectives: Describe where people were and how situations felt in the past.
Describe completed past actions with regular verbs and time markers.
grammarTopics: was/were in statements, negatives, and questions
regular past -ed and pronunciation patterns
went, had, saw, made, took, came, and bought
did/didn't plus base verb
past simple sequence with time expressions
integrated past simple review
communicativeFunctions: Describe where people were and how situations felt in the past.
Describe completed past actions with regular verbs and time markers.
Use frequent irregular past forms in a short account.
Ask and answer about completed past actions.

units.title: Stories & Experiences
units.description: Set a scene, connect events, and discuss basic life experiences.
objectives: Describe an action that was in progress at a past moment.
Connect a continuing background action with a shorter past event.
grammarTopics: past continuous was/were plus -ing
past continuous with while and past simple with when
past tenses with first, then, suddenly, and finally
present perfect with ever and never
present perfect experience plus past simple detail
integrated past and present perfect review
communicativeFunctions: Describe an action that was in progress at a past moment.
Connect a continuing background action with a shorter past event.
Organize a short story with a beginning, sequence, and ending.
Ask and answer about life experience without a finished time.

units.title: Plans & the Future
units.description: Express intentions, arrangements, decisions, predictions, and possibilities.
objectives: State planned intentions based on a decision already made.
Discuss fixed personal arrangements with time and place details.
grammarTopics: be going to plus base verb
present continuous for arranged future events
will plus base verb and contractions
will and going to for predictions
might/may plus base verb and maybe
integrated future forms review
communicativeFunctions: State planned intentions based on a decision already made.
Discuss fixed personal arrangements with time and place details.
Make an immediate decision, offer help, or state a neutral future fact.
Make and explain simple predictions about the future.

units.title: Comparing & Choosing
units.description: Compare people and options, describe extremes, and make a reasoned choice.
objectives: Compare two people, places, or products using common comparative forms.
Identify an extreme or top option in a group.
grammarTopics: comparatives with -er, more, and irregular better
superlatives with the -est, the most, and the best
as adjective as and not as adjective as
too much/many and not enough
comparative linkers and because
integrated comparison review
communicativeFunctions: Compare two people, places, or products using common comparative forms.
Identify an extreme or top option in a group.
Describe equal and unequal qualities in two options.
Explain why an amount or quality does not fit a need.

units.title: Travel & Accommodation
units.description: Navigate travel services, request information, and solve common airport and hotel problems.
objectives: Find a gate, understand basic departure information, and answer check-in questions.
Check in at a hotel and confirm a reservation and room details.
grammarTopics: travel questions and airport instructions
polite requests and reservation details
indirect polite questions with could and can
present/past facts with problem and request language
present perfect with just, already, and yet
integrated travel and present perfect review
communicativeFunctions: Find a gate, understand basic departure information, and answer check-in questions.
Check in at a hotel and confirm a reservation and room details.
Request and clarify times, platforms, locations, and prices.
Report a delay, missing item, or reservation problem and request action.

units.title: Work, Study & Responsibilities
units.description: Discuss work and study duties, rules, advice, and personal goals.
objectives: Describe current work or study and the main tasks involved.
Explain external duties and things that are not necessary.
grammarTopics: present simple and work/study vocabulary
have to/don't have to for obligation
must and mustn't for rules
should/shouldn't plus base verb
to-infinitive for purpose and want to
integrated obligation, advice, and purpose review
communicativeFunctions: Describe current work or study and the main tasks involved.
Explain external duties and things that are not necessary.
State strong rules and prohibitions clearly.
Ask for and give practical work or study advice.

units.title: Health & Everyday Problems
units.description: Describe common symptoms, request pharmacy help, give advice, and discuss likely results.
objectives: Name major body parts and locate simple pain or discomfort.
Describe common symptoms and answer basic follow-up questions.
grammarTopics: body nouns and possessive forms
have plus symptom and feel plus adjective
polite requests and quantity/frequency language
should/shouldn't for advice
first conditional if plus present, will plus base
integrated symptom, advice, and conditional review
communicativeFunctions: Name major body parts and locate simple pain or discomfort.
Describe common symptoms and answer basic follow-up questions.
Ask a pharmacist for a suitable non-emergency product and understand basic directions.
Give and respond to sensible everyday health advice.

units.title: Opinions, Technology & Social Life
units.description: Express opinions, respond respectfully, describe things with relative clauses, and arrange social plans.
objectives: State a clear opinion and support it with a simple reason.
Respond to an opinion with respectful agreement or disagreement.
grammarTopics: I think, in my opinion, and because
agreement phrases and polite contrast
basic relative clauses with who, that, and where
relative clauses and present tense integration
future arrangements and invitation language
integrated A2 tense and function review
communicativeFunctions: State a clear opinion and support it with a simple reason.
Respond to an opinion with respectful agreement or disagreement.
Add identifying information about a person, thing, or place.
Describe how a device or app helps or creates an everyday problem.
